name: July 31, 2026 Joint DPRK IT Worker Alert

attribution.legal_posture: Joint detection and mitigation guidance covers unnamed workers, actors, employers, accounts, and front companies.

ttps: KVM hardware and remote desktop access
caveats: Applicant identity documents, personal contact details, and private interview recordings stay out of the public dataset.
Every listed behavior is a signal requiring corroboration before supporting DPRK affiliation.
The alert states that indicators should be evaluated in combination; behavior-level signals gain meaning through corroboration.
This is a local-language official mirror of the multinational alert; it remains a single campaign source family.

statements: The German Foreign Office provides a complete German-language official version of the July 2026 multinational alert. Its practical value is localized compliance and hiring guidance: strong document checks, in-person interviews where appropriate, anomaly detection across account data, checking payee/name mismatches, shared identity documents or IPs, suspiciously long sessions or work hours, fake self-reviews, manipulated video, team-operated accounts, cryptocurrency payment requests, and operations concealed from Southeast Asian or African locations.

sources.support: The German Foreign Office publishes the official German-language version of the July 31, 2026 multinational alert, localizing combined-signal checks for identity and payee mismatches, shared identity or network artifacts, manipulated video or interview proxies, team-operated accounts, cryptocurrency requests, and location concealment
sources.locator: Full German-language warning; sections describing operating methods and account/application warning signs

sources.support: The alert says no specific behavior proves DPRK affiliation and recommends verification of identity, biometrics, location, employment/education, payments, devices, IP telemetry, logs, and sanctions screening
sources.locator: PDF pp. 2–6, especially Guideline #1 and Appendix

value.statement: NK News reports the 11-country joint alert about DPRK IT-worker revenue generation.

sources.quote: The 11 member states of a multilateral initiative monitoring DPRK sanctions evasion issued a joint alert for the first time on Friday about North Korean information technology (IT) workers’ illicit revenue generation activities.

value.statement: NK News reports North Korea’s rejection of the 11-country IT-worker alert.

sources.quote: North Korea on Tuesday condemned a recent alert issued by 11 countries about Pyongyang’s information technology (IT) worker operations, dismissing the allegations as a politically motivated attempt by the U.S. and its allies to “tarnish” the country’s image.
